content: The system shall allow authenticated users to apply a discount code at checkout. The discount shall reduce the order total by the percentage specified in the discount record.
A discount code may not be applied to orders with a total below $10.00.
Discount code: A string of 6–12 alphanumeric characters issued by the marketing team to reduce order price.
Document revision history: v1.0 (2025-01-10, initial draft), v1.1 (2025-03-05, added section 4), v1.2 (2025-04-02, added cart limits, shipping & tax, and stakeholders sections).
For example, if the user has a 20% discount code and their cart totals $50, the discount reduces the total to $40.
Checkout Service — Requirements Specification
Document owner: Commerce Platform Team. Classification: Internal.
Order total: The sum of all line-item prices in a customer's cart, prior to tax and shipping, expressed in USD.
Cart: A collection of one or more line items a customer intends to purchase, persisted per user session.
SKU: Stock Keeping Unit — a unique alphanumeric identifier for a purchasable product variant.
Tax rate: The percentage of an order's subtotal charged as sales tax, determined by the shipping destination's jurisdiction.

This document describes the requirements for the checkout service's discount code feature. It covers eligibility, application rules, and the acceptance criteria that govern discount behavior at checkout.
A discount code may only be applied once per order.
The system shall display the applied discount code and percentage on the checkout summary before order confirmation.
The system shall prevent checkout when the cart contains zero items.
A single order may contain a maximum of 20 distinct line items.
The quantity of any single SKU in a cart shall not exceed 99 units.
For example, if a customer attempts to add a 100th unit of the same SKU, the system rejects the addition and displays a quantity-limit error.
The system shall calculate sales tax based on the shipping address's jurisdiction tax rate at the time of checkout.
Orders shipped to addresses outside the United States are not eligible for standard shipping and shall default to international shipping rates.
For example, an order with an $80.00 subtotal shipped to a jurisdiction with a 7.5% tax rate incurs $6.00 in sales tax, for an order total of $86.00.
Stakeholders: Jane Doe (Product Owner, Commerce Platform), Raj Patel (Engineering Lead), Priya Nair (QA Lead). Approval status: Approved by Commerce Platform Steering Committee on 2025-03-10.
User Account & Authentication — Requirements Specification
Document owner: Identity & Access Team. Classification: Confidential.
Document revision history: v1.0 (2024-11-02, initial draft), v2.0 (2025-02-18, added multi-factor authentication requirements).
Session token: An opaque, server-issued credential that authenticates a user's browser session after successful login.
Multi-factor authentication (MFA): A login process requiring two or more independent verification factors.
Account lockout: A temporary suspension of login capability for an account, triggered by repeated failed authentication attempts.
Password reset token: A single-use, time-limited credential issued to verify a user's identity during a password reset flow.
This document describes requirements for user account authentication, including login, multi-factor authentication, account lockout, and password reset flows.
The system shall lock a user account after 5 consecutive failed login attempts within a 15-minute window.
An account lockout shall persist for a minimum of 30 minutes before the user may attempt to log in again.
The system shall notify a user by email when their account is locked due to failed login attempts.
Failed login attempts shall reset to zero after a successful login.
For example, if a user enters an incorrect password 5 times between 2:00pm and 2:10pm, the account is locked until at least 2:40pm.
The system shall require multi-factor authentication for accounts with administrator privileges.
MFA codes delivered via SMS shall expire 5 minutes after issuance.
The system shall allow users to register at least one authenticator app as an MFA method.
MFA cannot be disabled on accounts with administrator privileges.
For example, an administrator logging in receives a 6-digit MFA code by SMS that must be entered within 5 minutes or a new code must be requested.
The system shall allow a user to request a password reset link via their registered email address.
Password reset links shall expire 1 hour after issuance.
Password reset links are single-use: once a link has been used to reset a password, it is no longer valid for any subsequent request.
The system shall require a new password to differ from the user's previous 5 passwords.
For example, if a user requests a password reset at 9:00am, the reset link becomes invalid at 10:00am even if unused.
The system shall expire a user's session token after 30 minutes of inactivity.
Session tokens are not valid after the user has logged out; a logged-out session token cannot be used to authenticate any further request.
Idle timeout: The duration of user inactivity after which a session is automatically terminated.
The system shall allow a user to view and revoke active sessions from their account settings.
Stakeholders: Alex Kim (Security Lead), Morgan Lee (Product Owner, Identity & Access), Sam Torres (QA Lead). Approval status: Approved by the Security Review Board on 2025-02-20.
